newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel steady but major buyer absent.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel steady but major buyer absent.

text.p: NWE low sulphur straight-run was steady in talk on Monday but buying interest thinned a little after a refiner stopped his search for a July loader to go transatlantic, traders said.
A refiner was heard offering at $105 fob for 0.5-0.7 pct sulphur material with one active buyer on the market at $3 to $4 lower.
Traders said that an independent U.S. refinery was heard to have abandoned its quest for a fourth cargo to top up three ones bought earlier this month which were destined for the United States.
"They said it is too expensive for them as fuel prices are too high these days," one trader said, adding they have already loaded two of the three cargoes.

A second trader said the refiner was mulling selling one of the 25,000 tonne cargoes bought earlier as taking it to the States would be uneconomical with high freight rates, but may come back in if a seller can put together a 50,000-tonne loader.
"They could not combine it (cargo) with anything else...To take 25,000 (tonnes) to the States, freight will kill it," the trader said.
A seller said he was not offering as he was running different crudes and he was waiting to see the quality of the material he will be offering before asking a price.
Russian high sulphur straight run continues to be scarce on the E-4 and M-40 front, with only one cargo of the latter loading soon and none seen of the former.
M-100, of which five or six cargoes will load soon, was on offer at a steady two means plus $2/$2.50 while M-40 was valued at two means plus $5/$6.
